Each call decides one value: take it or leave it. That gives 2ⁿ subsets for n values, and the empty set has one subset, the empty one, which the base case produces by copying an empty

un-chooses so the second branch starts from the same state the first one did. Without the

Building the answer costs O(n·2ⁿ) time, because each of the 2ⁿ subsets is copied into
and a copy is up to n long. Beyond the result, the function uses
, which never holds more than n values, and the call stack, which is n + 1 frames deep: O(n) extra space. Interviewers ask for both numbers, and the recursion stack is the half that people leave out.

You pass with a recursion that handles the empty input, says 2ⁿ, and counts the stack in the space. Correct code with "O(2ⁿ) space" and no mention of the stack depth is a partial pass. A version that forgets the un-choose, or that answers 2ⁿ − 1 because it skips the empty subset, is a fail.

Recursion is a function that calls itself, and each live call owns a stack frame, a block on the thread's stack holding its parameters, locals and the address to return to, so every recursion has two numbers, not one: how many calls it makes, the time, and how deep the calls nest at once, the memory. They move independently. A search that fans out into millions of calls can still nest only a few dozen deep, while a plain "process one element, then recurse on the rest" makes exactly as many calls as it nests.

It's the right reach for a genuine tree of decisions: subsets, permutations, bracket generation, any search where you choose one option, explore everything that follows, then undo the choice so the next option starts from the same state, the choose-explore-unchoose rhythm. That undo is what lets one shared, mutable container serve the whole search instead of a fresh copy at every node. It's the wrong reach, dressed as recursion, when the shape is really a straight line down the input: its depth grows with the input size, and C++ gives no guarantee that the compiler turns it back into a loop, tail call or not; that depends on the compiler and the flags.

Every recursion needs a base case it answers without calling itself, and progress toward it on every call; missing either is a crash, not a wrong answer. Backtracking adds pruning: a test that rejects a partial answer before its subtree is built, which leaves the worst case unchanged but lowers what real inputs cost.

The mistake that shows up under pressure is a recursion whose depth tracks the input size, correct at every base case and step, that a reviewer signs off on because nothing looks wrong. It runs fine in every test, because the tests are short, then runs out of stack the day the input is long, crashing at a line that reads like ordinary arithmetic. The fix moves the pending work off the call stack: a one-call-per-level recursion becomes a plain loop, and a branching one becomes a loop over an explicit stack kept on the heap, where the depth can no longer overflow anything.
You meet this in the interview question itself: generate every subset of a small set by recursion, and give both numbers an interviewer expects, the call count and the stack depth, not one alone.

The other failure is the one that reaches production. This function does nothing a reviewer would stop at:
AddressSanitizer reports a stack-overflow with a backtrace of a little under 250 identical

frames, between 244 and 248 over repeated runs. It keeps at most 256 entries and the unwinder gives up a few short of that, so the exact count drifts with the stack layout. Either way, what you see is the top of the pile, and the million frames below it are never printed. The base case and the progress are both correct, so no test on a short path fails; the depth is the length of the input, and this input is a million long. The numbers from the theory section apply: the same function returned at 42,000 segments under the sanitizers and at 130,000 without them. A robot that logs its path for an hour and then asks for its length crashes at a line that looks like arithmetic. Stack overflow is not something the language detects: built without the sanitizers, the same program dies with the shell printing
